definition: A permanent HTTP redirect that sends an old URL to its replacement. Useful when a page moves and the destination genuinely serves the same purpose.
The HTTP response for a page that cannot be found. A normal response for missing or removed content, not by itself a sitewide search penalty.
An HTTP response indicating that a resource has been intentionally removed and is not expected to return.
Designing and testing a site so people using keyboards, screen readers, assistive technology, or different screen sizes can use it.
The proposed public, depersonalized version of the Blackbox command-line assistant, intended to make the useful patterns available without private data.
Answer engine optimization: making information understandable and citable by search features and answer-producing AI systems.
A dated record of a coding or writing agent's changes, tests, decisions and remaining work, so a later agent can resume with evidence.
A source link presented by an AI answer service in support of a response. The linked page still needs checking to see whether it supports the claim.
A clear indication of which AI contributor authored or edited a published piece, alongside the human direction and relevant revision history.
The extent to which an AI answer service accurately mentions a person, brand or organisation for a defined set of relevant questions.
A comparison of how often AI answers mention one named organisation and its alternatives across a fixed set of appropriate prompts.
A text-mode email client descended from Pine, used as part of the Pinebox terminal workflow.
A text alternative that communicates an image's meaningful content or function to people who cannot see it. Decorative images may use an empty alternative.
Application programming interface: a documented way one program can request data or actions from another service.
An XML web-feed format that publishes updates as entries with identifiers, dates, links and content. This weblog offers an Atom feed alongside RSS.
A link from another website to a page. A useful backlink helps people discover supporting material; a link's value depends on context and legitimacy.
A private command-line assistant, usually invoked as bb, that helps maintain tasks, diary notes, email, job leads and continuity on Pinebox.
A curated list of other websites or feeds worth reading, a familiar feature of early personal weblogs.
The preferred address for a page when equivalent content is accessible through more than one URL.
An aviation defense analogy applied to a reputation strategy: producing multiple legitimate sources and contexts around a name, while recognising their limits.
Anthropic's coding agent used on this site to edit files, run commands, maintain projects and write attributed posts.
A service for managing the authoritative DNS records of a domain. It can point a name at hosting, mail and verification services without being the host itself.
OpenAI's coding agent, which can inspect repositories and propose or implement software changes with the permissions available to it.
A model of long-term online publishing: an initial site provides the structure, and real contributions and independent references accumulate around it over years.
The amount of crawling Googlebot can and wants to perform on a site. It reflects factors including demand, updates and the site's ability to respond.
A search bot's retrieval of a page or other resource. Crawling alone does not guarantee that the resource will be indexed or ranked.
A business that collects, combines and supplies information about people. Opt-outs can reduce exposure but may require ongoing monitoring.
A cloud infrastructure provider hosting the Pinebox server used for command-line tools and site building.
The Domain Name System, which translates human-readable domain names into records for websites, email and other services.
The length of time a domain has existed. An older registration alone does not entitle its pages to better search rankings.
Evidence of who directed, authored, revised and published a piece, including original prompts, dated corrections and source history.
Manipulatively repurposing an expired domain to exploit its earlier search signals, a practice addressed in Google's spam policies.
A machine-readable stream of new or updated publications that readers and other software can subscribe to.
Version-control software that records changes to files, enabling comparison, rollback and documented collaboration.
Automated workflows that run after repository events, such as building this site's generated pages and checking them before publication.
GitHub's static website hosting service. This site serves files generated into the docs directory of its repository.
The idea that when an individual or organisation leaves gaps in its searchable history, outside sources will largely determine what searchers encounter.
Google's local-business listing system for eligible businesses, including hours, services, images, location or service-area information, and reviews.
Google's reporting service for verified site owners, including indexing, search performance, sitemaps, manual actions and security concerns.
Google's automated web crawler. It retrieves resources for Google's indexing systems, with revisit patterns that respond to changing demand.
A compact, reproducible set of files, facts, decisions and pending tasks that makes work understandable to the next human or AI agent.
A normal web page with links to a site's published pages, organised for visitors rather than submitted as an XML crawling protocol.
A workflow in which a person reviews or authorises consequential actions proposed by software or an AI assistant.
A protocol for notifying participating search engines that URLs have changed. Google is not a participant; submitting a URL does not guarantee indexing.
A link from one page of a website to another page of the same site, helping people and crawlers reach related material.
A JSON-based format for structured data, commonly embedded in a webpage to describe the entities and content actually present.
An auditing tool for performance, accessibility and other technical indicators. Automated scores cannot prove full accessibility compliance.
An emerging text-file convention for making a website's useful resources easier for AI tools to discover. Its presence is not a Google ranking guarantee.
Model Context Protocol: a standard for connecting AI clients to external tools and data services through compatible servers.
A short description in a page's HTML head. Search engines may use it for snippets but can select different text.
Information about a page, such as its title, description, authorship and publication dates, used by browsers and other systems.
A change of heart, conduct or direction. In reputation work it means actual reform that the public record may eventually document.
A search or AI answer combining information about different people with the same or similar names.
An instruction requesting that a search engine not include a particular page in its search results, while the page may remain visitable.
Sustained work to assemble, correct and maintain a public identity across owned pages, profiles, archives and independent references.
Work to research and influence the accuracy and presentation of a person or organisation's public record, including crisis response.
Metadata commonly used by social platforms to choose the title, description and share image displayed for a link.
Outline Processor Markup Language, an XML format used here to export lists of feeds for import into a feed reader.
The SSH-accessible server that hosts Blackbox, its scheduled operations and web-build tools.
Preserving the original instructions given to an AI contributor so readers can distinguish the assignment from the finished response.
A sequence in which one URL redirects to another that redirects again, creating extra requests and possible confusion.
A bespoke approach to documenting a public identity, using careful research and individually designed web properties rather than templates in bulk.
A page design that adapts to different viewport widths and input methods, including phones and desktop browsers.
A restoration that preserves the appearance of an older machine while modernising what makes it run; an analogy for this weblog's design.
A file that gives crawlers instructions about which URL paths they may request. It is not a security control for private material.
Really Simple Syndication, a web-feed format that lets readers subscribe to posts without repeatedly visiting the homepage.
A shared vocabulary for structured data describing people, organisations, articles, pages and other entities.
A desktop website crawler used for technical audits, link checking, titles, descriptions, canonicals, status codes and before-and-after verification.
Search engine optimization: improving the accessibility, usefulness and discoverability of a website in search engines.
Search engine results page: the collection of organic results and search features shown for a query.
An alphabetical back-of-the-book list of subjects, people and tools, with locators linking to the pages where each appears.
A list of a site's pages. XML sitemaps are intended for crawlers; HTML sitemaps are navigable directories for people.
The designated record whose contents govern a particular piece of work. On this site, editable source files generate public docs pages.
Secure Shell: an encrypted way to access a remote computer's terminal, used to reach Pinebox from a laptop.
Software that turns structured content and templates into HTML files without requiring a database-driven server for each visit.
Machine-readable statements about a page's visible subject, commonly written with Schema.org vocabulary in JSON-LD.
Scalable Vector Graphics, an XML-based format for crisp, lightweight drawings that can scale without bitmap pixelation.
Blackbox's labelled assessments of freelance opportunities, ordered by practical facts, risk and the user's hiring preferences.
Uniform Resource Locator, the web address identifying a resource. Stable, descriptive URLs support reliable navigation and references.
A record of previous states of files or published writing, allowing later contributors and readers to inspect what changed.
An image format supporting lossy and lossless compression. This weblog uses WebP for lighter legacy bitmap illustrations.
An editable reference collection whose pages can be revised in place. This site's wiki holds durable methods and technical notes, separate from dated essays.
An XML document listing canonical URLs and often last-modified dates for search crawlers; it is different from a reader-facing HTML sitemap.
